I have been farming these fields in Quzhou County my whole life. At 62 years old, I know what this land can do. Like every year, I will grow winter wheat and summer maize on the same 5 mu plot — that is the rotation that feeds my family and brings in cash. My wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, and now it is waking up. I will irrigate it three times: once to help it survive the spring dry spell, again at jointing, and once more at heading so the grain fills properly. For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer at the base and topdress with urea when the wheat starts to surge — about 18 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I will spray for weeds once, insects twice, and fungi once because the damp weather here invites disease. I use improved wheat seed like Luyuan 502, and I till the soil with a rotary tiller before sowing to break up the clods.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize — Deng Hai 605, the seed my neighbors all trust — using no-tillage direct seeding right into the wheat stubble. Maize grows fast and greedy, so I will give it about 16 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu, mostly as compound fertilizer at sowing with a side-dressing of urea at the big喇叭口 stage. I will irrigate twice if the rains are kind, three times if they are not. For pests, I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice; maize here does not usually need fungicide. I expect my wheat to yield around 500 kg per mu and my maize about 550 kg per mu, which is honest and reliable for this soil.
